<reason>B wins the comparative clash rather than merely defending curriculum oversight. A offers a plausible account of chilling effects, but repeatedly treats harmful content as bounded and correctable while making omissions effectively undetectable. B challenges both assumptions, explains how misleading curricula can spread and persist, and answers the pressure questions directly with appropriately qualified support. A concedes that justified political pressure counts, then shifts toward whether that pressure is safe rather than whether its collateral harm is greater. Its closing does not resolve B’s central challenge to the proposed ranking.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s strongest rebuttal asks why political pressure can hollow out assessments yet leave professional accuracy review reliably effective. This exposes A’s inconsistent assumptions about institutional correction. A’s closing treats that challenge as a concession about omissions instead of answering its comparative force.</best_rebuttal>
